ref: DAR — Daniel ch. 9: The Seventy Weeks
title: The Seventy Weeks
voicePrompt: In your own words, explain how this chapter argues that the seventy weeks are 'cut off' from the 2300 days of chapter 8, why the decree to Ezra in 457 B.C. is the starting point, and how the resulting dates point to Christ's baptism, crucifixion, and ultimately to 1844.

questions.stem: According to the chapter, how did Daniel come to understand that the seventy years of captivity were nearing their end?
options: Gabriel appeared to him in a dream and announced it directly
He understood by books — the writings of Jeremiah — that God would accomplish seventy years in the captivity
King Darius told him the captivity was about to be lifted
He calculated it from the vision of the ram and he-goat in chapter 8
questions.explanation: The chapter states Daniel 'understood by books, that is, the writings of Jeremiah, that God would accomplish seventy years in the captivity of his people,' citing Jeremiah 25:12 and 29:10. Gabriel comes only later, after Daniel's prayer.

questions.stem: The chapter argues that 'the vision at the beginning' to which Daniel refers (verse 21) is which earlier vision?
options: The vision of chapter 8 (the ram, he-goat, little horn, and 2300 days)
The interpretation of Nebuchadnezzar's dream image in chapter 2
The vision of the four beasts in chapter 7
A new vision given that same night in chapter 9
questions.explanation: The chapter reasons that chapter 8 is the only prior vision where Gabriel is named, where he is commanded to make Daniel understand, and which Daniel says he did not understand — so Gabriel returns in chapter 9 to complete that unfinished mission.

questions.stem: According to the chapter, what does the Hebrew word translated 'determined' in verse 24 ('Seventy weeks are determined') actually signify, and why does that matter?
options: It means 'fulfilled,' showing the seventy weeks were already complete
It means 'cut off,' so the seventy weeks must be cut off from the 2300 days of chapter 8
It means 'sealed,' so the seventy weeks were hidden from Daniel
It means 'doubled,' so the seventy weeks represent 980 years
questions.explanation: The chapter argues at length, citing Gesenius, Stockius, Hengstenberg, and the ancient versions, that the word 'properly' means 'cut off,' and that there is no period from which the seventy weeks could be cut off but the 2300 days of the previous vision — establishing the connection between chapters 8 and 9.

questions.stem: Of the four candidate decrees, which one does the chapter conclude is the true starting point for the seventy weeks, and in what year?
options: The decree of Cyrus, B.C. 536
The decree of Darius, B.C. 519
The decree of Artaxerxes to Ezra, B.C. 457
The commission to Nehemiah, B.C. 444
questions.explanation: The chapter rejects the decrees of Cyrus and Darius (preliminary, concerning the temple only) and Nehemiah's grant (merely verbal, only 52 days of work), concluding that the decree to Ezra in the seventh year of Artaxerxes, B.C. 457, alone meets every requirement of the prophecy.

questions.stem: Dating from B.C. 457, what event does the chapter say marks the end of the sixty-nine weeks (483 years), reaching to 'Messiah the Prince'?
options: The birth of Christ in B.C. 4
The baptism of Jesus and beginning of His public ministry in the autumn of A.D. 27
The crucifixion in the spring of A.D. 31
The martyrdom of Stephen in A.D. 34
questions.explanation: The chapter states that the sixty-nine weeks (483 years) dating from B.C. 457 end in A.D. 27, the year Jesus was baptized and the voice from heaven declared Him the beloved Son, after which He preached 'The time is fulfilled.'

questions.stem: According to the chapter, what happened 'in the midst' of the seventieth week, and in what year?
options: The decree to Ezra went forth, in B.C. 457
Jerusalem's wall was finished, in B.C. 408
The Messiah was cut off (the crucifixion), in the spring of A.D. 31
The gospel turned to the Gentiles, in A.D. 34
questions.explanation: The chapter argues that 'midst' means 'middle,' locating the crucifixion in the middle of the seventieth week, in the spring of A.D. 31 — three and a half years after the baptism in autumn A.D. 27 — supported by thirteen credible authorities. There the sacrifice and oblation virtually ceased.

questions.stem: How does the chapter connect the close of the seventy weeks to the end of the 2300 days?
options: The seventy weeks and the 2300 days end at the same time, in A.D. 34
The seventy weeks (490 years) are the first portion of the 2300; subtracting 490 leaves 1810, which added to autumn A.D. 34 gives autumn A.D. 1844
The 2300 days are literal days, so they ended only six and a half years after the decree
The 2300 days began at the crucifixion in A.D. 31 and ran for 2300 literal years
questions.explanation: The chapter states the seventy weeks (490 years) ended in autumn A.D. 34; taking 490 from 2300 leaves 1810; adding 1810 years to autumn A.D. 34 brings the termination of the whole period to the autumn of A.D. 1844, when the sanctuary cleansing of chapter 8:14 begins.

questions.stem: According to the chapter's note, what does 'to anoint the most Holy' (verse 24) refer to?
options: The anointing of the Messiah Himself at His baptism
The crowning of Christ as king after the resurrection
The anointing of the heavenly sanctuary, marking the opening of Christ's ministration there
The rebuilding and rededication of the earthly temple in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: The chapter argues that the Hebrew 'kodesh kodashim' (holy of holies) is never applied to a person, and refers to the anointing of the heavenly sanctuary before Christ's ministration begins there — the last event of the seventy weeks — not to the Messiah Himself.
